note: Poorly defined. A birthday gives purpose but does not support the praise for atmosphere. Ask which detail explains why the visit took place and what the opening would lose without it. Specify an objective checked answer, retries and support.

Objectively answerable. The phrase is itself the affordability judgement, not a supporting exact price. Ask learners to select what the writer judges and distinguish the named food from absent prices. Check and give targeted feedback.

Objectively answerable. The quiet corner helps the group talk without raising voices. Provide several plausible effects and ask which follows from that detail. Record whether independently correct or supported.

Poorly defined within the current paragraph. Earlier crowding evidence is needed for the editor's note. Show the two extracts together and ask which earlier detail gives a reason for going off peak. Check selection.

Objectively answerable. The price helps a student decide whether lunch fits a budget. Avoid treating a quoted price alone as proof of value. Match price and distance to cost and travel decisions. Replace completion by length.

Objectively answerable. Time on court makes a filling portion relevant to an active reader. Ask why the writer adds that experience, with flavour and sharing as alternative effects. Use checked recognition.

Objectively answerable. The music impedes conversation after seating, whereas the queue delays seating. Match each drawback to its effect. Feedback should separate the two and explain what both mean for friends.
Poorly defined in isolation. To test advice grounded in evidence, display the preceding music observation. Ask which reader benefits from earlier timing. Use checked selection and support.

Poorly defined. The distant planet establishes genre and setting but does not justify the opening praise. Ask which plot detail sets up the story without revealing an ending. Consider optional placement because the book opening already tests this.

Objectively answerable. Quiet conversations show hopes and fears, supporting lifelike characters. Pair that detail with the relevant praise and contrast practical effects or plot speed. Check the link directly.

Objectively answerable. Tension makes the ending exciting despite the slow middle. Select the reason the judgement stays positive and explain that it does not fix the pacing. Checked feedback distinguishes the two effects.

Legitimately open-ended if rewritten. Ask the student to write one recommendation for a named reader with a different preference, borrowing one fact. Separate the first attempt and self-review against a model. The current prompt asks for an already explicit audience link.

Objectively answerable. The hidden map starts the mystery without giving away its outcome. Compare two openings with different levels of plot detail and check which preserves suspense. Avoid duplicating the film opening.

Objectively answerable. Similar characters make dialogue confusing. Match each of the paragraph's two judgements to its own evidence and effect. Improved feedback should contrast the vivid settings with the confusing dialogue.
Objectively answerable. Discoveries keep the reader interested, while short chapters affect pace. Give an evidence-to-verdict matching task and record supported versus independent completion.

Poorly defined. The reason for attending is given without a judgement to support. Make optional as an opening-purpose question or ask learners to connect the motivation with the later recommendation for local music fans. Check the link using both extracts.

Poorly defined. Workshops illustrate what to do between concerts rather than supporting a stated opinion. Ask which detail helps someone decide whether they can try music themselves. Use checked recognition or combine with the preceding opening investigation.

Objectively answerable. Waiting in heat makes the queues uncomfortable. Let students select the effect and match it to the wait, alongside the contrasting audience response to the band. Replace the length gate with meaningful checked work.

Poorly defined without the previous paragraph. Bring the water-queue detail into the task. Match bringing a bottle and arriving early to their separate purposes. Give feedback about the difference between advice and evidence.

Objectively answerable. A range of skill levels matters to someone unsure whether they can take part. Show two reader profiles and ask which concern the evidence addresses. Avoid implying every course suits every visitor.

Objectively answerable. The demonstrations build confidence rather than make the course physically easier. Use a short cause-and-effect match and explain how confidence supports praise of the instructors.

Legitimately open-ended when focused. Ask students to weigh included equipment and repeat attempts for a named reader on a budget. Keep uncertainty about actual price and preserve “most courses”. Compare against a model and record self-review.

Poorly defined in isolation. Packed lunch addresses the menu, not physical suitability. Pair the earlier menu sentence with the advice, then check which drawback it responds to. Consider making optional because the festival advice tests a similar link.

Poorly defined. Collecting tools describes gameplay without establishing fun. Ask which bit of description tells players what they will do, or pair the first paragraph with the next to connect tools and the writer's enjoyment.

Objectively answerable. The combined tools unlock hidden areas and make success rewarding. Select the example that supports clever puzzle design and show why other details describe rather than evaluate.

Objectively answerable. Repetition is an effect of unclear directions for inexperienced players. Ask which proposed improvement would reduce that effect. Consider making optional because the switch tutorial workshop later develops the same idea.

Legitimately open-ended with a revised brief. Ask for one line of advice for students playing during short journeys. Short levels support this; high scores address another preference. Use comparison and self-review, with the reasoning shown in the example.

Objectively answerable. Practical experiments are compared with textbooks for memorability. Ask which claim the contrast supports, while distinguishing the writer's opinion from a universal rule. Check and explain the distinction.

Objectively answerable. Building bridges involves testing ideas; clear explanations help beginners. Let students match each of these facts with a different judgement. Give feedback that preserves both roles.

Poorly defined as a cross-paragraph inference without the crowding detail. Show it alongside the close and ask how fewer visitors affect opportunities to try experiments. Check the reasoning and offer support after an unsuccessful attempt.
